problem:
Consider the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{3}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

activity_context.topic_title: Solving 3x3 Singular Systems of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-z=-1 \\ y+3z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-z=-1 \\ y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution. 

From the first equation, we get

$$
x-z=-1\,⇒\,x=-1+z
$$

and from the second equation, we obtain

$$
y+3z=1\,⇒\,y=1-3z.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+z \\ y=1-3z \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1+z \\ 1-3z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
